Write a C++ program that asks the user to input two integers, and then computes and displays the greatest common divisor (GCD) of them. Use a function to calculate the GCD using the Euclidean algorithm. Provide informative prompts and error handling for incorrect input (such as non-integer input, zero or negative values). Ensure proper formatting and readability of the code by including comments, appropriate variable names, and indentation.<|im_end|>

```C++
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

int gcd(int a, int b) {   // function to calculate GCD using Euclidean algorithm
  if (b == 0) {
    return a;
  }
  else {
    return gcd(b, a % b);
  }
}

int main() {
  int num1, num2;
  bool valid_input = true;   // flag to check if input is valid

  // ask user to input two integers
  cout << "Enter two integers to find their greatest common divisor (GCD):\n";
  // loop to ensure input validation
  do {
    valid_input = true;
    // check input for non-integer values
    if (!(cin >> num1 >> num2)) {
      cout << "Error: Invalid input. Please enter valid integers.\n";
      cin.clear();
      cin.ignore(numeric_limits<streamsize>::max(), '\n');
      valid_input = false;
    }
    // check input for zero or negative values
    else if (num1 <= 0 || num2 <= 0) {
      cout << "Error: Invalid input. Please enter positive non-zero integers.\n";
      valid_input = false;
    }
  } while (!valid_input);   // repeat until input is valid

  // compute and display GCD of the input integers
  cout << "The GCD of " << num1 << " and " << num2 << " is " << gcd(num1, num2) << ".\n";

  return 0;
}
```
